canonical_execution_convention.collector_status: selected as an execution convention, not as a demonstrated superior collector

decision_gate.reason: No single retained mechanism strongly explains both timing and the three-seed sign pattern. The evidence instead shows coupled, trajectory-dependent PID, behavior, entropy, and optimization paths.

missing: per-episode actor tensors and parameter norms

available: raw retained diagnostic episodes at each scientific checkpoint

finalizer_recovery_audit.qualification: The retained manifest is a single state record rather than an external append-only invocation log. Its timestamps, six one-pass artifacts, hashes, and aggregation-only recovery source are mutually consistent.

mechanism_ranking.reason: PID timing and immediate update amplification are direct, and seed-specific lambda/regime paths accompany outcomes; no exogenous PID feature uniquely reproduces the sign reversal.
Final log-alpha separation orders with outcome deterioration and T47 shows an entropy rebound, but alpha is jointly endogenous.
Some loss scale separation appears in seeds 29/47, but retained snapshots show no uniquely timed collapse and omit targets.
Seed 47 has 30 more EPISODIC completed tasks yet the worst EPISODIC outcome, defeating a simple exposure account.
The treatment contrast is exact and large but essentially fixed across seeds, so it cannot alone identify the sign reversal.
Scheduling and occupancy are retained; sampled indices and ages are not.

missing_field_ledger.field: sampled replay indices and transition IDs
missing_field_ledger.impact: No empirical sample-age or recent-window fractions.
No per-episode actor L2 drift; hashes and update counts only.
Abrupt sub-checkpoint optimization transients cannot be located.
Checkpoint scalar losses cannot diagnose calibration/collapse.
Zero row contains learner initialization only; no episode inferred.
Single manifest open/completion record plus six sealed files and recovery code establish consistency, but not an external audit log.

H1.confidence: HIGH for timing; LOW for causal attribution
H1.effect_direction: EPISODIC immediate block exposure and generally higher volatility
H1.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H1.evidence_supporting_mechanism: EPISODIC has greater speed/deadline jump volatility and applies all updates immediately after PID; this can explain stronger feedback, but the same contrast exists in losing seeds.

H2.effect_direction: EPISODIC fixed; TRANSITIONAL changes within episode
H2.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H2.evidence_supporting_mechanism: EPISODIC makes zero actor updates during collection versus about 129 per TRANSITIONAL episode; fixed-policy trajectories may reduce within-task drift, but this does not identify the favorable sign.

H3.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H3.evidence_supporting_mechanism: All EPISODIC updates see a complete just-finished episode versus a tiny terminal fraction under TRANSITIONAL; sampled indices are absent.

H4.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H4.evidence_supporting_mechanism: EPISODIC completes 10 more episodes and has shorter episodes, a direction compatible with its +3 result here only.

H5.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H5.evidence_supporting_mechanism: Both oscillate; EPISODIC finishes diagnostic FEASIBLE (12/18 RSR) while TRANSITIONAL is MIXED (9/18), matching Validation's +3.

H6.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H6.evidence_supporting_mechanism: Final alpha is similar (EPISODIC slightly lower); exploration does not provide a clear seed-11 advantage.

H7.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H7.evidence_supporting_mechanism: Checkpoint actor and critic losses decline smoothly in both; no unique collapse precedes the +3 result.

H1.effect_direction: EPISODIC immediate block exposure and generally higher volatility

H1.evidence_supporting_mechanism: EPISODIC again has higher multiplier volatility and immediate PID exposure, but that treatment-level fact does not uniquely explain -4.

H3.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H3.evidence_supporting_mechanism: Schedule-level freshness differs strongly; actual samples and ages were not logged, preventing attribution.

H4.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H4.evidence_supporting_mechanism: Episode counts and mean lengths are almost equal (236 versus 238), arguing against task exposure as the main seed-29 cause.

H5.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H5.evidence_supporting_mechanism: Both end MIXED on diagnostics; Validation shows EPISODIC completes more but loses deadline and speed compliance, an aggressive tradeoff.

H6.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H6.evidence_supporting_mechanism: EPISODIC ends at about half the TRANSITIONAL alpha, consistent with less late exploration but not causally identified.

H7.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H7.evidence_supporting_mechanism: TRANSITIONAL reward/constraint critic losses are much lower at the retained checkpoints, but snapshot losses are scale-sensitive and not direct error estimates.

H1.confidence: HIGH for timing; LOW for causal attribution
H1.effect_direction: EPISODIC immediate block exposure and generally higher volatility
H1.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H1.evidence_supporting_mechanism: EPISODIC's immediate PID exposure and higher speed-lambda volatility coexist with a late collapse; deadline volatility itself is similar.

H2.effect_direction: EPISODIC fixed; TRANSITIONAL changes within episode
H2.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H2.evidence_supporting_mechanism: TRANSITIONAL performs about 145 actor updates during an average episode and recovers late; whether nonstationarity causes recovery is not separable from replay and PID timing.

H3.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H3.evidence_supporting_mechanism: The schedules sharply differ, but missing sample indices make actual freshness and episode amplification unmeasurable.

H4.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H4.evidence_supporting_mechanism: EPISODIC exposes 30 more completed tasks and shorter episodes yet loses by 7, directly contradicting a simple diversity/exposure benefit.

H5.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H5.evidence_supporting_mechanism: EPISODIC leads at 100k-150k, is FEASIBLE-dominant at 250k, then falls to CRAWLING/PARTIAL at 300k; TRANSITIONAL recovers after 150k.

H6.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H6.evidence_supporting_mechanism: TRANSITIONAL alpha rebounds after 150k and ends about 8.7x EPISODIC; this is consistent with recovery, not proof that entropy caused it.

H7.evidence_against_mechanism: The same collector-level contrast occurs in seeds with the opposite RSR direction, or the required fine-grained evidence was not retained.
H7.evidence_supporting_mechanism: EPISODIC critic losses exceed TRANSITIONAL snapshots while behavior later degrades, but no per-update trace or target statistics remain.

sign_reversal_analysis.conclusion: No exogenous mechanism variable changes sign in a uniquely identifying way. Final deadline lambda matches the outcome signs, but is itself an endogenous summary of the diverged trajectories.

features.interpretation: EPISODIC is more volatile for all seeds; the sign does not reverse.
The small seed-47 reversal does not reproduce the RSR ordering.
The intended schedule contrast is nearly invariant across seeds.
Seed 47 contradicts a simple more-episodes explanation.
Episode-length direction is not concordant across all seeds.
Final speed multipliers are higher under EPISODIC for all seeds.
This is the only compact internal feature with matching signs and ordering, but it is an endogenous result of episode costs.

sign_reversal_analysis.method: Descriptive sign/order concordance only; n=3 and no inferential statistics.
